summary: Dickson County tower built by the CCC in 1935-36 for TDF; moved about 12 miles to Towerview Farm, Houston County, in 1997.

facts.design: Aermotor tower, 70 ft, with a 7 by 7 ft metal cab; 14 by 24 ft chestnut log cabin built as the towerman's residence
facts.status_note: Moved intact by truck about 12 miles in 1997 to Towerview Farm, Houston County. Tennessee Landforms lists the Stony Point entry as moved. No source describes the original site today.

access.note: The register names Joel and Jason Clark as owners and administrators of Towerview Farm and describes no public visiting arrangement.

events.note: Built by the CCC in 1935-36 for the Tennessee Division of Forestry at Stoney Point, Dickson County (register wording).
Bought by Joel and Jason Clark and moved intact by truck about 12 miles to Towerview Farm, with the chestnut cabin.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on March 1, 1998.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Tennessee Landforms spells the site Stony Point; the register spells it Stoney Point. Both describe the Dickson County CCC tower built for TDF, so the story uses Stony Point and notes the spelling.

notes_for_editor: Two sources: the Tennessee Landforms listing (moved) and the register entry, which the owners nominated, so the move is the owners' own account. The register coordinates (36.2802, -87.5721) are for the farm; the record's coordinates (36.2638, -87.511) come from Tennessee Landforms and presumably mark the original site. Record agency is blank; the register says TDF built it, so the editor may want TDF as the agency at construction. Suggested other_names: Towerview Fire Tower, Stoney Point. Whether the tower is still at the farm in 2026 was not checked; the register entry dates from 1998. No source describes the original site today.
